drill_count_prompt: How many points is this trick worth?
drill_count_explain: {sum} = **{total}** points. Remember: A 11, 10 10, K 4, D 3, B 2, everything else 0.
drill_count_hint: Add them one by one: A is 11, 10 is 10, K is 4, D is 3, B is 2; 7, 8 and 9 count nothing.
drill_trumps_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. Tap every trump in this hand.
drill_trumps_explain_suit: The four Buben are always trumps, plus every card of {suit}.
drill_trumps_explain_grand: In Grand only the four Buben are trumps; all four suits are equal.
drill_trumps_hint_suit: Don't forget the Buben — whatever suit is printed on them, they are trumps.
drill_order_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. Tap these cards from highest to lowest.
drill_order_explain_null: In Null the order is the "natural" one: {order}.
drill_order_explain: {order}. The Buben come first, ranked ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦, then A, 10, K, D, 9, 8, 7.
drill_order_hint_null: Null has no trumps; a Bube is an ordinary card: A, K, D, B, 10, 9, 8, 7.
drill_order_hint: Think: the Buben are highest (♣ ♠ ♥ ♦), then A, 10, K, D, 9, 8, 7.
drill_legal_prompt: The game is **{contract}** and an opponent leads **{lead}**. Which of your cards may you play? Tap them all.
drill_legal_explain_any: You have no {led}, so any card is allowed.
drill_legal_explain_follow_trump: The lead is {led}, and if you have them you must follow. Buben are trumps too: you may — and must — follow with them.
drill_legal_explain_follow_suit: The lead is {led}, and if you have that suit you must follow. A Bube is not part of the suit and cannot be used to follow.
drill_legal_hint: First ask: which suit does the lead count as? (Hint: {led}) Do you hold any of it?
drill_winner_why_top_trump: {card} is the highest trump in the trick.
drill_winner_why_only_trump: {card} is a trump, and a trump beats every side card.
drill_winner_why_suit: Nobody played a trump and {suit} was led, so {card}, the highest card of that suit, wins. Other suits don't count, however high.
drill_winner_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. The three cards were played from left to right. Which one wins the trick?
drill_winner_hint: First look for trumps. If there are none, only cards of the suit that was led can win.
drill_matador_prompt: The game is **{contract}**. How many matadors does this hand have?
drill_matador_explain_with: You hold ♣B, so you are "with". Count down from ♣B until the first trump you **don't** have: {n} in a row.
drill_matador_explain_without: You don't hold ♣B, so you are "without". Count down from ♣B the trumps you are **missing**, until the first one you have: {n} in a row.
drill_matador_hint: Look only at the top card, ♣B: holding it means "with", missing it means "without". Then count the unbroken run down ♣B ♠B ♥B ♦B A 10 K…
drill_value_prompt: You want to play **{contract}**. If you win, what is the game worth — in other words, how high can you bid?
drill_value_prompt_hand: You want to play **{contract}**, and as a **Hand** game (without looking at the skat). If you win, what is the game worth — in other words, how high can you bid?
drill_value_explain: {matadors}, game +1 → multiplier {mult}. The base value of {contract} is {base}, so {base} × {mult} = **{value}**.
drill_value_explain_hand: {matadors}, game +1, Hand +1 → multiplier {mult}. The base value of {contract} is {base}, so {base} × {mult} = **{value}**.
drill_value_hint: Game value = base value × multiplier. Multiplier = matadors + 1 (game) + any extras. Base values: ♦9 ♥10 ♠11 ♣12 Grand 24.
drill_settle_win_prompt: The declarer plays {name} with multiplier {mult} (game value {value}) and ends with **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_lose_prompt: The declarer plays {name} with multiplier {mult} (game value {value}) and ends with only **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_lose_tie: 60 is a tie, and a tie counts as a loss for the declarer.
drill_settle_schneider_prompt: The declarer plays {name}; before play the multiplier was {mult}. It goes very well: **{pts}** card points. What does the declarer score?
drill_settle_schneider_explain: {pts} ≥ 90 is **Schneider**, which adds 1 to the multiplier: {base} × {mult} = **+{score}**.
drill_settle_overbid_prompt: The declarer bid up to **{bid}** and plays {name}. After play it turns out the multiplier is only {mult} (game value {value}). The declarer took 70 card points. What is the score?
drill_settle_overbid_explain: A game value of {value} is below the bid of {bid}: that is an **overbid**, lost whatever the card points. It is scored at the smallest multiple that covers the bid, {base} × {mult} = {bid}, and doubled: **{score}**.
drill_settle_hint: First decide won or lost (61 card points; an overbid always loses). Won scores +game value, lost scores −2 × game value.

skat_hint_pickup_covers: **Pick up the skat**: on average it improves a hand by about one card, and you get to put two useless cards away — Lina and Noah always pick it up when they declare. Without the skat, this hand would be worth {value} as **{contract} Hand**, which covers your bid of {bid}; you can risk Hand (multiplier +1), but you will neither see the skat nor put anything away.
skat_hint_pickup_short: **Pick up the skat**: on average it improves a hand by about one card, and you get to put two useless cards away — Lina and Noah always pick it up when they declare. Without the skat, the best this hand could play is {contract} Hand, worth {value} — below your bid of {bid}, so Hand now would be an overbid.

about_meta_title: About SkatGo – how the daily Skat and private tables work
about_meta_description: Questions about SkatGo answered: is it free, do you need an account, how scoring works, which rules apply, how the daily Skat and private tables work.
about_daily_1: Every day brings new cards for two competitions: 1 deal today, which anyone can play without an account, and a tournament of {n} deals with your free SkatGo account. Everyone gets the same cards in the same seat against the same two AI opponents, so you can compare what you made of each hand. You play each once a day; a new day begins at midnight in Berlin.
about_daily_2: Every deal is scored by Seeger-Fabian and added to your day’s total. After each deal you see how the AI played the same cards from your seat, and its score.
about_daily_3: Each competition has its own leaderboard for every day, ranked by Seeger-Fabian total, with the AI’s total on it for comparison; you can look back over the last seven days. You stand on it at once when you finish, under the nickname you set in the settings or a random one. The tournament also gives every player an Elo rating.
about_learn: New to Skat? The free course takes you through the cards, trump order, bidding and scoring step by step and ends with a complete game. The rules cover contracts, following suit and game values, with examples to look up.
about_friends_1: Open a table with your free account, enter your name and send the invite link to up to two friends. They sit down with just a name – no sign-up, no app. Start once everyone is there; the AI takes any empty seat.
about_friends_2: You play by the International Skat Order, without Kontra, Re, Ramsch and Bock, as many games in a row as you like, and everyone sees all three Seeger-Fabian scores. If someone loses their connection, the AI plays on for them until they come back through the same link.
faq_free_a: Yes. Every lesson and every game against the AI is free.
faq_account_a: Not to learn or to play freely: your progress is saved in your browser, and signing in is optional. The tournament of six deals needs a free account.
faq_score_a: In free play, a won game scores its game value and a lost game costs twice its value. The daily tournament uses Seeger-Fabian: a won declarer game adds 50, a lost one costs another 50 on top of the doubled loss and gives each defender 40.
faq_rules_a: The international Skat rules (ISkO): bidding, suit games, Grand and Null, Hand, Schneider, Schwarz and Ouvert. Kontra/Re, Ramsch and Bock are not played. If everyone passes, free play deals again; in the tournament, the passed-in deal scores 0.
faq_phone_q: Can I play on my phone?
faq_phone_a: Yes. SkatGo runs in the browser on phones, tablets and computers, with nothing to install.

bidding_how_title: How to work out your bid
bidding_how_text: For suit games and Grand: **bid value = base value × multiplier**. The multiplier counts your matadors ("with" or "without" so many), plus 1 for "game" and 1 each for Hand, Schneider, Schneider announced, Schwarz, Schwarz announced and Ouvert. That takes a suit game to a multiplier of at most {suit}, and Grand to {grand}. Null is not multiplied; it has fixed values.
